title: Nominations
text: Nominations - Shocktoberfest Court The Shocktoberfest Court will consist of 12 students, two from each academic college, who serve as role models for the entire university community. Student elected to the court must exhibit qualities such as strong leadership, good character, loyalty to Wichita State, and true Shocker Pride. Court members will be interviewed by a panel of Wichita State faculty and staff and two students will selected to hold the title of Shocker Royal! Nominate a Candidate The Shocktoberfest Committee encourages students, faculty, and staff to nominate students who: positively represent Wichita State University play an active role on-campus in an organization, group, and/or position of leadership promotes belonging and Shocker Pride demonstrate academic excellence Nominations will close on Friday, September 5 at midnight. Nominate a Student Application for Court Candidate Requirements Currently enrolled, full-time, degree-seeking students 30 or more credit hours completed as of August 2025 2.75 GPA or higher Good academic and conduct standing with Wichita State Please note, Student Engagement & Belonging reserves the right to remove any court member who is not in good standing with or whose conduct reflects poorly on Wichita State University. Process for Nominees All nominees who meet the requirements of the Shocktoberfest Court will be asked to submit an application. All applications will be reviewed by the staff of Student Engagement & Belonging resulting in a selection of 24 applications to be reviewed by a panel of Wichita State University faculty/staff. The panel will score applications resulting in up to 12 members to represent the Shocktoberfest Court. On Tuesday, Sep. 23, members of the court will be announced and voting will begin. Wichita State students may cast one ballot each. The ballot will close on Wednesday, Oct. 1. Court members will attend and participate in Shocktoberfest events. At Shocker Madness, two students will be crowned and given the title of Shocker Royalty! Obligations Those selected as court members will be required to participate in the Shocktoberfest Parade and attend Shocker Madness on Saturday, October 4. Professional attire will be required for the parade and Shocker Madness. The presence of the court will also be requested at events throughout the week including the Kick-Off, Bonfire, and The Roast. Each applicant must understand that these appearances are mandatory, and by accepting a position on the Shocktoberfest Court, are agreeing to fulfill them.

title: Shocktoberfest Spirit Competition
text: Shocktoberfest Spirit Competition - Shocktoberfest Competitions Shocktoberfest is a time to embrace what it means to be a Shocker! The spirit competition represents camaraderie, community and a sense of belonging. There are multiple ways for students, groups, faculty/staff, and the community to join in on a few fun and friendly competitions. Page Navigation Individual Competitions Spirit Competition Registration Form COMPETITIONS The following list of competitions are eligible for individual event registrations. There are opportunities for individual students, faculty, staff, and departments, and student organizations. We hope you find something that works for you and your schedule. Groups wishing to compete in the multiple events including the Parade should visit the Spirit Competition section. Banner Decorating Competition Groups will decorate a 4'x8' banner to be displayed around campus. Winning group to receive a $100 award. Who can compete | Any student group and/or Spirit Competition Teams General Information The banner competition is designed to display the creative skills and abilities of WSU students by creating an artistic banner showcasing Shocker pride at Wichita State University. A 4’ (long) x 8’ (wide) vinyl banner with grommets (holes) must be used. Groups will be provided a banner on a first-come, first-serve basis. Groups should use waterproof materials and keep the banner 2D because the banner may be displayed in an outdoor location. Please refrain from using glitter. The Traditions Committee reserves the right to discontinue the display of a banner if it does not sufficiently withstand the weather conditions. Although the utmost care will be taken with the banners, the Traditions Committee cannot assume responsibility for banners with wet paint or materials adhered to them nor can we ensure the safety of your banner as they are displayed publicly with limited security. Once Shocktoberfest is over, banners will be available for pick up between Wednesday, October 9 – Tuesday, October 15, in SE&B Office, RSC Room 216. Banners are not picked up during this time will become property of SE&B and may be discarded. Rules On Theme: Shocktoberfest is a "Blast from the Past" and should celebrate life at Wichita State through the decades. Pick a time period since WSU's founding to highlight in your banner. Banners are due Tuesday, September 24 by 5 p.m. in SE&B Office, RSC Room 216 . Banners that are turned in after 5 p.m. may be hung but will not be judged. The Traditions Committee will determine if any late banners will be hung. No computer generated artwork will be allowed on the banners. The Traditions Committee reserves the right not to display any banner that is deemed inappropriate. Requirements The banner will focus on "Blast from the Past" and should celebrate life at Wichita State through the decades. Pick a time period since WSU's founding to highlight in your banner. The name of the sponsoring group must be clearly seen and spelled out on the banner. (Greek letters are allowed, but the organization’s name must still be spelled out.) Shocktoberfest 2025 must appear somewhere on the banner. Banner Scoring Rubric Judging Criteria Point Range with 10 being the highest Originality/Creativity 0-10 Correlation to Theme "Blast from the Past" 0-10 Quality of Workmanship 0-10 Meets the Requirements 0-10 Overall Impression 0-10 Maximum Points 50 Registration is captured on one form listed at the end of this page. Department Door Decorating Competition Departments are encouraged to show their Shocker Pride and celebrate Shocktoberfest . The winning department will receive $100 towards an office party. Who can compete | WSU Departments General Information Any WSU department may compete by decorating a doorway, wall, or entryway on to promote both Shocktoberfest and school spirit. This years theme is " Amber Wave's of Grain ". Departments will utilize the theme to emphasize Shocker Pride . Decorations must include Shocktoberfest 2025 Judging will take place the week of Shocktoberfest and you will be notified in at least 24 hours in advanced of the judging committee’s arrival. The office of the winning door will receive an office party valued at $100 to be arranged at a later date. Individual award recipients will receive a $50 Shocker Store Gift Card. Rules Department Door decorations must be finished by Friday, September 26 at 5 p.m. and remain on display through Monday, Oct. 6. Use materials that will not damage doors and/or walls. Painters tape is recommended. Use caution when using/removing command strips. The door used must remain fully operational with decoration. All materials should be flame resistant. Trees and greenery must be artificial and flame resistant. Any lights used must by UL - approved and low wattage. Fire alarm pull stations, fire extinguisher cabinets, smoke detectors, and exit signs must not be covered and exits must not be blocked. No cords for electricity or other purposes are allowed under doors or across/in hallways. Requirements The decoration should celebrate Wichita State Shocker Pride and may incorporate the theme “Amber Waves of Grain” Shocktoberfest 2025 must appear somewhere on the decoration. Door Decorating Scoring Rubric Judging Criteria Point Range with 10 being the highest Originality/Creativity 0-10 Correlation to Theme 0-10 Quality of Workmanship 0-10 Meets the Requirements 0-10 Overall Impression 0-10 Maximum Points 50 Registration is captured on one form listed at the end of this page. Pickleball Competition Wednesday, October 1 | 6 - 9 p.m. Heskett Pickleball Courts Who can compete | Individual Faculty/Staff, On-Campus Residents, Departments, Spirit Teams Rules Teams must registered by Tuesday, September 23 at midnight Shocktoberfest Committee will accept the first 16 teams and will notify all applicants. Tournament will be played in doubles and teams may have between 2 and 6 players on their roster. All matches will be Doubles and played as single sex or co-ed. Matches will be played in best two out of three to 11 points, win by 1 or 2 points. Single elimination with a consolation bracket Teams will switch court sides at the end of each game. If the teams play a 3rd game, teams will switch at 6 points. It is preferred that players bring their own equipment but equipment will be available for use free to players. Requirements All players must wear close toed shoes. All players must be present at the scheduled time of play Prize 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place winners will receive a trophy. Spirit Competition Teams who place will receive a trophy and the top three teams will receive points as noted below. Individuals may only represent a Spirit Team or RSO, they can not sign in for both. Individuals who sign in for both will be disqualified and removed from the competition. Parade Individuals, groups, departments, and community are welcome to enter the Shocktoberfest Parade. Accepted entries include but are not limited to walking units, dance teams, decorated cars, carts, and floats. title: Shocktoberfest Parade
text: Shocktoberfest Parade - 2025 Shocktoberfest Parade Saturday, October 4 | 4 pm Everyone is invited to attend the Shocktoberfest Parade, the highlight of the weeklong celebration of Shocker spirit and pride. Participants will enjoy entertainment from the Shocker Sound Machine marching band, dance teams, and decorated cars and floats from student groups, WSU departments and community members. Shocktoberfest is a university wide initiative coordinated by WSU Foundation and Alumni Engagement and Student Affairs Guest Information Parade Route Parade Registration Guest Information Shockers of all ages are invited to attend the Shocktoberfest Parade. This event is open to WSU students, faculty/staff, alumni, family, friends, and of course the Wichita community. Bring a lawn chair, snacks, and get ready to view the talents of Shocker Nation. Parking The parade will kick off at the Marcus Welcome Center, heading West on Mike Oatman DR, taking a right on Perimeter RD finishing at Koch Arena. Visitor parking is located throughout campus and can be viewed on the interactive parade map. Recommended Parking Lots: 19W, 5, 10, 2W, and 1. text: Shocktoberfest Events - Click image to go to the interactive map 2025 Schedule of Events MONDAY | TUESDAY | WEDNESDAY | THURSDAY | FRIDAY | SATURDAY MULTI-DAY EVENTS Banners on Display Monday, Sep. 29 – Sunday, Oct. 5 On display around campus Cost : Free Students competing in the Shocktoberfest spirit competition have decorated banners celebrating Shocker Pride. Bonfire Monday, Sep. 29 | 7 p.m. Braeburn Square Cost : Free Revel in the spirit of Shocktoberfest with WSU Cheer, Marching Band and a few of your favorite athletes. Faculty/Staff who are interested in attending will receive a food voucher in exchange for two canned food items to be donated to the Shocker Support Locker. Want to be a vendor? title: Overall Trophy Rules
text: Overall Trophy Rules - Shocktoberfest utilizes three divisions for most competitions: Men’s Division, Women’s Division, and Co-Ed Division. Events incorporating the divisions award 1st, 2nd and 3rd place in each division. All other events are awarded participation points. Groups competing for the Overall Trophy must submit a master roster to be eligible. Rosters are found in the Shocktoberfest Application Packet. Only individuals listed on the team’s master roster will be permitted to participate in events, including participation events, if the group is competing for the overall trophy. Groups may only enter one team in each activity, except basketball where two teams will be allowed, one in the Shocktoberfest participation division and one in the open division. Individuals cannot be on more than one master roster per division. Only groups competing for the overall trophy are eligible to receive the points assigned to each event. Individuals or teams not competing for the overall trophy and only competing in single events are still eligible to win the cash prizes and individual trophies assigned to each event. a. Example- Team A, Team B, and Team C are competing for the overall trophy and Team D is not. Team D finishes 1st place in Banner Competition, Team A finishes 2nd, Team B finishes 3rd and Team C finishes 4th. Team D will be awarded the first place trophy for Banner Competition but Team A will receive the 1st place points toward the overall trophy, Team B will receive the 2nd place points, and Team C will receive the 3rd place points. A team does not have to compete in every Shocktoberfest event to be eligible to win the Overall Trophy, but they must compete in Songfest. Points from all events participated in will be totaled to determine the Shocktoberfest Overall Trophy winner in each division and will be presented at the Awards Ceremony following Songfest. Teams placing 1st, 2nd or 3rd in any event will not be eligible to receive participation points in addition to placing points for that event. In the event of a tie for the Overall Trophy in any division, the team with the most 1st place finishes throughout the Shocktoberfest competitions will be named the winner. If a tie remains, then 2nd place finishes will be counted. If a tie still remains, then 3rd place finishes will be counted. If a tie still remains, the team which participated in the most events will be named the winner.

title: Shocktoberfest History
text: Shocktoberfest History - Since 1991 Shocktoberfest has been Wichita State’s annual celebration of Shocker spirit and pride. Beyond uniting Shockers through events and programs, many competitions are offered in which groups come together to compete for the Shocktoberfest trophy, standing over five feet tall. Over the years Shocktoberfest has seen many events come and go as the needs and interests of students have changed. The most recent addition to Shocktoberfest includes the WSU sponsored Pumpkin Run, a program which brings together Shockers from all ages from the campus and community to participate in a registered 5K and walk. In 2012, Shocktoberfest moved further into the month of October and left behind Mud Events, which still remains a long standing SAC tradition, now hosted in September. Active competitions are always a feature and have included events like 3 on 3 basketball and dodge ball. 2007 was the last year of a video competition which was replaced with Songfest in 2008, a lip syncing and dance competition that now concludes Shocktoberfest. Prior to being hosted by the Student Activities Council, Shocktoberfest was a picnic sponsored by the Alumni Association that took place during Homecoming week. In 1979, the picnic was referred to as the Pre-Game Homecoming Picnic. Over the years, the picnic grew from being just food and drinks before the game to being one of the biggest parties on campus. In addition to the event’s activities growing and changing over the years, so did the name for the picnic. In 1982, Alumni renamed the event “Oktoberfest” featuring a German theme that included a polka band, dancers, and other German specialties. According to findings in WSU publications, 2000 people attended the first Oktoberfest. In 1983, the event became “Shocker Oktoberfest” followed by “Shocktoberfest” in 1984. While the event continued to grow, the name “Shocktoberfest” remained. Following the 1986 football season, the football program ended after 16 years of struggling to rebuild after the plane crash of 1970. While campus continued Homecoming in 1987, even in the absence of a football team, Shocktoberfest suffered and became a much smaller event. By 1988, the Alumni Association had discontinued Shocktoberfest altogether. As the campus continued the celebration of WSU spirit, Homecoming morphed and changed. In 1990, Homecoming was turned over to the Student Activities Council who, in 1991, brought a drastic change to the program. SAC decided to change Homecoming into a fall festival called “Shocktoberfest,” a week that still played host to some of the more traditional events during Homecoming such as mud volleyball, but also incorporated many new activities. Over the next few years, as Shocktoberfest evolved, many other events were added to celebrate WSU pride. In addition to new events, the concept of Homecoming Royalty was replaced with Man and Woman of the Year in 1992. Man and Woman of the Year now serves as a stand-alone event hosted by Student Involvement. The love of being a Shocker is not only for students and does not leave once you receive your diploma. The pride runs deep and so does tradition. In spring of 2010, the Alumni Association, with the support of its membership, brought back Homecoming to the WSU campus. With the tradition of Homecoming restored, Shocktoberfest still remains as the main spirit celebration for the Wichita State Campus. Go Shocks!

title: National Pan-Hellenic Council
text: National Pan-Hellenic Council - Shock the Yard Step Show The National Pan-Hellenic Council of Wichita State University is proud to present the most exciting event of the year, the NPHC Step Show. WSU NPHC fraternities and sororities are excited to present a talented explosion of themed step and stroll routines. What is Stepping? Stepping is an expressive performance art that also functions as a ritual of group identity for many of the nine (9) NPHC organizations represented on various collegiate campuses. The NPHC Step Show in an interactive experience that draws the audience into various stories, exciting dance moves, and stunts. 12th Annual Shock the Yard Step Show Saturday, April 18, 2026 6 p.m. | Charles Koch Arena Doors open at 5 p.m. Ticket Rates Coming Soon Perform at the Step Show Accepting performances from collegiate and community based groups and organizations. title: Wichita State Fraternity and Sorority Life Celebrates Academic Excellence at Scholarship Reception
text: Wichita State Fraternity and Sorority Life Celebrates Academic Excellence at Scholarship Reception - Matthew “MatPat” Patrick, a YouTube creator and entrepreneur known for the popular “Game Theory” series, will speak at Wichita State University at 7 p.m. Thursday, April 16, in Lowe Auditorium at the Eugene M. Hughes Metropolitan Complex. Doors open at 6:15 p.m. Tickets prices are $10 for WSU students, $18 for WSU faculty/staff and $25 for the general public. Tickets are available at wichita.edu/sac . This event is intended for ages 13 and older. During the event, Patrick will present a talk about his career as a content creator, gaming theorist and entrepreneur. The talk will be followed by a moderated question-and-answer session. Patrick, aka MatPat, is the founder and former host of the “Theory” Channels on YouTube, one of digital video's best-known and most successful brands. With over 45 million subscribers and 9 billion total views, MatPat’s channels are best described as modern-day Mythbusters, educating viewers on science, math and critical thought through the lens of pop culture. His creative work also spans larger-scale productions like producing the YouTube Premium series Game Lab, as well as Creators in Fashion, the first-ever live fashion week for creator-founded apparel brands. He has hosted the reality competition show The Runner (executive producers Matt Damon and Ben Affleck), voiced a Transformer and made a surprise cameo appearance in Blumhouse's Five Nights at Freddy's movie. He also helped co-produce the Tony-nominated Broadway play Grey House as well as the West End musical Your Lie in April. MatPat is a respected digital strategist who, over the past decade, has deeply shaped the online discourse around the creator economy and online creator culture. After selling his business in 2022, Matt successfully transitioned his YouTube channels to a new series of hosts in 2024, pioneering a playbook for longevity of creator-led brands in the digital ecosystem. He’s also presented everywhere from Capitol Hill to the United Nations, engaging in creative collaborations with prominent world leaders and celebrities from Bill Gates to the Pope. But of all his work, he’s most proud of having used his platform to raise over $7 million for various charitable organizations. An Evening with MatPat is coordinated by WSU’s Student Activities Council (SAC) in collaboration with Shocker Studios. SAC is a student-led group charged with shaping campus culture through hosting unique experiences and memorable events. Student leaders gain transferable skills that prepare them for their future career pursuits. title: Wichita State Fraternity and Sorority Life Celebrates Academic Excellence at Scholarship Reception
text: Wichita State Fraternity and Sorority Life Celebrates Academic Excellence at Scholarship Reception - In celebration of National Literacy Week in March, Wichita State University’s Community Service Board (CSB) led a student driven project focused on supporting early childhood literacy in the Shocker Neighborhood. What started as a campus book drive turned into a larger service project centered around access to books for young readers. Students were invited to donate children’s books which resulted in 258 books collected across campus. These books will be donated to Kids’ World, an early childhood development center in the Shocker Neighborhood, along with a Little Free Library created and designed by students. The project was a collaborative effort led by Shocker Neighborhood Chair Matthew Cannon alongside members of the Community Service Board. CSB member Lillith Shook designed and hand painted the Little Free Library while Civic Engagement Graduate Assistant Haley Ensz also assisted with painting and bringing the final design together. The finished library reflects both the creativity and care that went into the project while also serving as a lasting resource for families in the area. In addition to collecting books, the project gave students the opportunity to create something meaningful that will continue serving the community beyond a single event or donation. The Little Free Library is intended to encourage reading and provide children and families with easier access to books close to home. The completed library and collected books will be delivered to Kids’ World on Wednesday at 3 p.m. This project highlights Wichita State students’ commitment to community engagement and finding hands on ways to support and connect with the Wichita community. ### COMMUNITY SERVICE BOARD Contact Us 1845 Fairmount St. Box 73 Wichita, Kansas 67260 SEB@wichita.edu (316) 978-3022 Get Connected SE&B on Instagram SE&B on Facebook SE&B on X

title: Communication Guidelines
text: Communication Guidelines - Guidelines for Official Communications with Government Officials University employees, when acting or purporting to act in a representative or official capacity on behalf of or for Wichita State University, should first notify the executive director of Government Relations prior to initiating any contact with, or before responding to, any contacts, requests or inquiries made by any elected or appointed federal, state, and/or local governmental officials or their respective staffs. All University activities involving or related to said federal, state and/or local governmental officials or their respective staffs must be developed in advance consultation with the executive director to insure the University's official position is being properly and appropriately presented and/or to provide for a coordinated and professional response on behalf of the University and its various constituencies. Additionally, the executive director will assist in the University's compliance with applicable laws, regulations or ordinances concerning these types of communications or interactions. It is important to remember that when contacting public officials as a private citizen it is not appropriate to utilize university resources (letterhead, paper, computers, fax machines, etc.) or prepare any such materials during business hours. title: Mission
text: Mission - Our mission is to serve as the University's primary point of contact with elected and appointed local, state and federal government officials. The office develops strategies and activities to ensure consideration by federal, state and local government officials of university and other public proposals appropriations. In addition, it holds the charge of overseeing and implementing legislative and regulatory relationships with the Congress, State Legislature, City Council, County Commission, and governmental offices and agencies at all levels. This charge is carried out through the following goals: Seek and pursue opportunities to advance the research and public service mission of the university Identify and secure adequate financial support to allow the university to fulfill its metropolitan mission Provide an official point of contact for federal, state, and local elected and appointed officials Initiate and participate in the development of research and higher education policy discussions at the federal, state, and local levels Provide assistance to administration, faculty, and staff in working through the legislative process Monitor regulatory and legislative activities at all levels of government Maintain up-to-date or legislative information for use by university personnel
